> [!IMPORTANT] > **Android beta testers needed:** The official BookOrbit Android app is in closed testing. [Join the Google Play beta](https://github.com/bookorbit/bookorbit/issues/2001) and stay enrolled for at least 14 days to help unlock its public release.


BookOrbit

A self-hosted library and reading platform for ebooks, PDFs, audiobooks, and comics.

Overview • Live Demo • iOS & Apple Watch • Features • Quick Start • Managed Hosting • KOReader • Docs

--- ## 📚 What is BookOrbit? **[BookOrbit](https://bookorbit.app)** organizes your books and lets you enjoy them anywhere: on iPhone, Apple Watch, the web, Kobo, or KOReader. Your reading progress, highlights, and status stay synchronized, so you can start a chapter in one place and continue in another. Around that core sit 14 metadata providers, reading statistics and achievements, OPDS and Send-to-Kindle delivery, multi-user accounts with OIDC/SSO, and automatic sync out to Hardcover, Readwise, and StoryGraph. All of it runs on infrastructure you control. ## 🚀 Live Demo Try the live instance before you install. No account required. > **Note:** The demo includes a sample library of public domain books. Some administrative features are limited in the public demo. Self-hosting BookOrbit provides the full experience. ## 📱 BookOrbit for iPhone and Apple Watch Take your library anywhere with the official native BookOrbit app. Read ebooks, PDFs, and comics; stream or download audiobooks; use text to speech; and keep reading offline. The app connects directly to your self-hosted BookOrbit server, while Apple Watch brings downloaded audiobooks and synchronized playback progress to your wrist.
Requires BookOrbit v3.0.0 or later and iOS 26 or later. Apple Watch features require watchOS 26 or later.
Explore all 14 screenshots ### iPhone ### Apple Watch
## ✨ Features ### Reading Experience & Sync - **Built-in Web Readers**: Ebooks (EPUB, KEPUB, MOBI, AZW3, AZW, FB2), PDFs, comics (CBZ, CBR, CB7), and audiobooks (M4B, MP3, M4A, OPUS, OGG, FLAC), with no extra plugins required. - **Native iPhone & Apple Watch Apps**: Read, listen, download, upload, and synchronize with your BookOrbit server from a native, offline-capable iPhone app. Send audiobooks to Apple Watch for independent offline playback and later progress reconciliation. - **Three-Way Sync (Kobo + KOReader + BookOrbit)**: Progress and annotations flow bidirectionally between Kobo devices, KOReader, and the BookOrbit web reader. Pick up on any surface where you left off on another, including highlights and deletions. - **KOReader Plugin**: An on-device catalog browser with search, download, and status and rating management, alongside full progress and annotation sync. - **Annotations & Highlights**: Highlights from the web reader, KOReader, and Kobo merge into one searchable hub. Filter by color, style, and source; export as Markdown, CSV, or JSON. - **Hardcover, Readwise & StoryGraph Sync**: Push status, progress, reading dates, and ratings to Hardcover on configurable triggers; status and progress to The StoryGraph; and new highlights and notes to Readwise as you create them, from both the web reader and synced devices. Hardcover read history can be pulled back to backfill blank BookOrbit entries. - **Statistics, Goals & Achievements**: Daily reading time, heatmaps, streaks, and library health, plus yearly goals, monthly challenges, and 50+ achievements across five categories. Reading DNA profiles your reading style from your actual session history. ### Library Management - **Multiple Libraries**: Isolate content with per-library folders, custom scan rules, and format priorities. - **12 Metadata Providers**: Google Books, Open Library, Amazon, Goodreads, Kobo, Hardcover, Audible, Audnexus, Libro.fm, and iTunes, plus ComicVine for comics and RanobeDB for light novels. [External providers](docs/METADATA_PROVIDERS.md) add more, such as Douban, FantLab, J-Novel Club, Libris, LubimyCzytac and MangaBaka. Cover art is sourced separately from iTunes, DuckDuckGo, and AudiobookCovers. - **Smart Scopes & Collections**: Organize your collection with curated lists and dynamic, rule-based saved filters. ### Platform & Delivery - **Multi-User & SSO**: Granular per-user permissions and isolated reading data, with native support for Authentik, Keycloak, and Authelia via OIDC. - **Multilingual Interface**: Community translations are managed on [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/bookorbit). See the [localization guide](docs/LOCALIZATION.md) for current language support and contributor instructions. - **Content Delivery**: OPDS support for compatible apps, Send-to-Kindle via email, and browser drag-and-drop uploads. - **Automated Ingestion**: Configure a Book Dock drop folder for hands-free importing. ## 🐳 Quick Start (Docker) ```bash mkdir bookorbit && cd bookorbit mkdir -p books data/app data/postgres curl -fsSLo .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bookorbit/bookorbit/main/.env.example curl -fsSLo docker-compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bookorbit/bookorbit/main/docker-compose.yml ``` Edit `.env` and set these required values: ```dotenv APP_URL=http://your-server-ip:3000 # the URL you'll open in your browser BOOKS_HOST_PATH=./books # folder on your server where your book files live POSTGRES_PASSWORD= # database password - openssl rand -hex 24 JWT_SECRET= # signs login tokens - openssl rand -hex 32 SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN= # one-time setup wizard token - openssl rand -hex 16 ``` If your local book folder is owned by a user other than UID 1000, also set `PUID` and `PGID` to match that owner. Getting these wrong is the most common cause of permission errors on first scan. Then start: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` Open `http://your-server-ip:3000` and complete setup using your `SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`. For the full installation guide including reverse proxy setup, host file permissions, secrets from mounted files, external databases, OIDC hardening, and environment variable reference, see **[bookorbit.app/installation](https://bookorbit.app/installation)**. ## ☁️ Managed Hosting Prefer a hosted instance without managing Docker or servers? [Zenith offers BookOrbit hosting](https://zenith.hosting/host/bookorbit) with a web file browser for uploads, access controls, and resource usage insights. ## 📖 How I Actually Use BookOrbit One read-along EPUB3 per book: listened to on iPhone, carried offline to Apple Watch for runs, read on a Kobo through KOReader, and picked up again on the laptop. One file, one reading position, no reconciling an audiobook against an ebook. Read the full walkthrough at **[bookorbit.app/my-workflow](https://bookorbit.app/my-workflow)**. ## 🔄 KOReader Plugin The BookOrbit plugin for KOReader adds progress sync, two-way annotation sync, and a native catalog browser: navigate, search, and download books from your library without leaving the device. 1. In BookOrbit, go to **Settings > KOReader**, create credentials if prompted, and click **Download Plugin**. 2. Unzip `bookorbit.koplugin.zip`. 3. Copy `bookorbit.koplugin` to `koreader/plugins/` on the device. 4. Restart KOReader and open a book. 5. Use **Tools > BookOrbit Sync** to connect. The download is pre-configured with your server URL and credentials, so there is no manual entry on the device. For full setup and sync options, see **[bookorbit.app/koreader-plugin](https://bookorbit.app/koreader-plugin)**. ## 🛠️ Documentation and Contributing Full documentation lives at **[bookorbit.app](https://bookorbit.app/what-is-bookorbit)**: libraries, metadata, readers, Kobo sync, OPDS, users and permissions, OIDC and more. **Guides** - **Book requests**: indexers, download clients, path mappings, automation and the encryption key they need. See the [book requests guide](https://bookorbit.app/book-requests/). - **Read-aloud**: optional STAlign generation and QuartzNet hardware acceleration. See [docs/READ_ALOUD.md](docs/READ_ALOUD.md). - **External metadata providers**: add a source that runs beside BookOrbit, such as FantLab or MangaBaka, with [docs/METADATA_PROVIDERS.md](docs/METADATA_PROVIDERS.md), or build your own with [docs/BUILDING_METADATA_PROVIDERS.md](docs/BUILDING_METADATA_PROVIDERS.md). **Contributing** - **Local development**: architecture, first-time setup, running, testing and conventions in [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). - **Contributing**: branch naming, test expectations, the PR checklist and commit format in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## ❤️ Support BookOrbit BookOrbit is built and maintained independently. Behind what appears to be a single product is a growing ecosystem: the core server and web application, Kobo and KOReader integrations, native iPhone and Apple Watch apps, and an Android app currently in development. Each part requires its own engineering, testing, compatibility, release, and support work. Keeping the entire ecosystem moving at its current pace, without compromising quality, requires considerable time, focus, and energy. Support helps make that pace sustainable and creates more room for thoughtful development. If BookOrbit is valuable to you and you would like to support its continued development, you can: - [Get the official iPhone and Apple Watch app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bookorbit-the-official-app/id6811807346) - [Support BookOrbit on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/neonbookorbit) - [Contribute through Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/bookorbit) - [Star BookOrbit on GitHub](https://github.com/bookorbit/bookorbit) Financial support is entirely optional. Important

Android beta testers needed: The official BookOrbit Android app is in closed testing. Join the Google Play beta and stay enrolled for at least 14 days to help unlock its public release.


BookOrbit

A self-hosted library and reading platform for ebooks, PDFs, audiobooks, and comics.

Overview • Live Demo • iOS & Apple Watch • Features • Quick Start • Managed Hosting • KOReader • Docs

📚 What is BookOrbit?

BookOrbit organizes your books and lets you enjoy them anywhere: on iPhone, Apple Watch, the web, Kobo, or KOReader. Your reading progress, highlights, and status stay synchronized, so you can start a chapter in one place and continue in another.

Around that core sit 14 metadata providers, reading statistics and achievements, OPDS and Send-to-Kindle delivery, multi-user accounts with OIDC/SSO, and automatic sync out to Hardcover, Readwise, and StoryGraph. All of it runs on infrastructure you control.

🚀 Live Demo

Try the live instance before you install. No account required.

Note: The demo includes a sample library of public domain books. Some administrative features are limited in the public demo. Self-hosting BookOrbit provides the full experience.

📱 BookOrbit for iPhone and Apple Watch

Take your library anywhere with the official native BookOrbit app. Read ebooks, PDFs, and comics; stream or download audiobooks; use text to speech; and keep reading offline. The app connects directly to your self-hosted BookOrbit server, while Apple Watch brings downloaded audiobooks and synchronized playback progress to your wrist.

Requires BookOrbit v3.0.0 or later and iOS 26 or later. Apple Watch features require watchOS 26 or later.

Explore all 14 screenshots

iPhone

Apple Watch

✨ Features

Reading Experience & Sync

  • Built-in Web Readers: Ebooks (EPUB, KEPUB, MOBI, AZW3, AZW, FB2), PDFs, comics (CBZ, CBR, CB7), and audiobooks (M4B, MP3, M4A, OPUS, OGG, FLAC), with no extra plugins required.
  • Native iPhone & Apple Watch Apps: Read, listen, download, upload, and synchronize with your BookOrbit server from a native, offline-capable iPhone app. Send audiobooks to Apple Watch for independent offline playback and later progress reconciliation.
  • Three-Way Sync (Kobo + KOReader + BookOrbit): Progress and annotations flow bidirectionally between Kobo devices, KOReader, and the BookOrbit web reader. Pick up on any surface where you left off on another, including highlights and deletions.
  • KOReader Plugin: An on-device catalog browser with search, download, and status and rating management, alongside full progress and annotation sync.
  • Annotations & Highlights: Highlights from the web reader, KOReader, and Kobo merge into one searchable hub. Filter by color, style, and source; export as Markdown, CSV, or JSON.
  • Hardcover, Readwise & StoryGraph Sync: Push status, progress, reading dates, and ratings to Hardcover on configurable triggers; status and progress to The StoryGraph; and new highlights and notes to Readwise as you create them, from both the web reader and synced devices. Hardcover read history can be pulled back to backfill blank BookOrbit entries.
  • Statistics, Goals & Achievements: Daily reading time, heatmaps, streaks, and library health, plus yearly goals, monthly challenges, and 50+ achievements across five categories. Reading DNA profiles your reading style from your actual session history.

Library Management

  • Multiple Libraries: Isolate content with per-library folders, custom scan rules, and format priorities.
  • 12 Metadata Providers: Google Books, Open Library, Amazon, Goodreads, Kobo, Hardcover, Audible, Audnexus, Libro.fm, and iTunes, plus ComicVine for comics and RanobeDB for light novels. External providers add more, such as Douban, FantLab, J-Novel Club, Libris, LubimyCzytac and MangaBaka. Cover art is sourced separately from iTunes, DuckDuckGo, and AudiobookCovers.
  • Smart Scopes & Collections: Organize your collection with curated lists and dynamic, rule-based saved filters.

Platform & Delivery

  • Multi-User & SSO: Granular per-user permissions and isolated reading data, with native support for Authentik, Keycloak, and Authelia via OIDC.
  • Multilingual Interface: Community translations are managed on Crowdin. See the localization guide for current language support and contributor instructions.
  • Content Delivery: OPDS support for compatible apps, Send-to-Kindle via email, and browser drag-and-drop uploads.
  • Automated Ingestion: Configure a Book Dock drop folder for hands-free importing.

🐳 Quick Start (Docker)

mkdir bookorbit && cd bookorbit
mkdir -p books data/app data/postgres
curl -fsSLo .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bookorbit/bookorbit/main/.env.example
curl -fsSLo docker-compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bookorbit/bookorbit/main/docker-compose.yml

Edit .env and set these required values:

APP_URL=http://your-server-ip:3000   # the URL you'll open in your browser
BOOKS_HOST_PATH=./books              # folder on your server where your book files live

POSTGRES_PASSWORD=         # database password           - openssl rand -hex 24
JWT_SECRET=                # signs login tokens          - openssl rand -hex 32
SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=     # one-time setup wizard token - openssl rand -hex 16

If your local book folder is owned by a user other than UID 1000, also set PUID and PGID to match that owner. Getting these wrong is the most common cause of permission errors on first scan.

Then start:

docker compose up -d

Open http://your-server-ip:3000 and complete setup using your SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN.

For the full installation guide including reverse proxy setup, host file permissions, secrets from mounted files, external databases, OIDC hardening, and environment variable reference, see bookorbit.app/installation.

☁️ Managed Hosting

Prefer a hosted instance without managing Docker or servers? Zenith offers BookOrbit hosting with a web file browser for uploads, access controls, and resource usage insights.

📖 How I Actually Use BookOrbit

One read-along EPUB3 per book: listened to on iPhone, carried offline to Apple Watch for runs, read on a Kobo through KOReader, and picked up again on the laptop. One file, one reading position, no reconciling an audiobook against an ebook.

Read the full walkthrough at bookorbit.app/my-workflow.

🔄 KOReader Plugin

The BookOrbit plugin for KOReader adds progress sync, two-way annotation sync, and a native catalog browser: navigate, search, and download books from your library without leaving the device.

  1. In BookOrbit, go to Settings > KOReader, create credentials if prompted, and click Download Plugin.
  2. Unzip bookorbit.koplugin.zip.
  3. Copy bookorbit.koplugin to koreader/plugins/ on the device.
  4. Restart KOReader and open a book.
  5. Use Tools > BookOrbit Sync to connect.

The download is pre-configured with your server URL and credentials, so there is no manual entry on the device. For full setup and sync options, see bookorbit.app/koreader-plugin.

🛠️ Documentation and Contributing

Full documentation lives at bookorbit.app: libraries, metadata, readers, Kobo sync, OPDS, users and permissions, OIDC and more.

Guides

  • Book requests: indexers, download clients, path mappings, automation and the encryption key they need. See the book requests guide.
  • Read-aloud: optional STAlign generation and QuartzNet hardware acceleration. See docs/READ_ALOUD.md.
  • External metadata providers: add a source that runs beside BookOrbit, such as FantLab or MangaBaka, with docs/METADATA_PROVIDERS.md, or build your own with docs/BUILDING_METADATA_PROVIDERS.md.

Contributing

  • Local development: architecture, first-time setup, running, testing and conventions in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
  • Contributing: branch naming, test expectations, the PR checklist and commit format in CONTRIBUTING.md.

❤️ Support BookOrbit

BookOrbit is built and maintained independently. Behind what appears to be a single product is a growing ecosystem: the core server and web application, Kobo and KOReader integrations, native iPhone and Apple Watch apps, and an Android app currently in development.

Each part requires its own engineering, testing, compatibility, release, and support work. Keeping the entire ecosystem moving at its current pace, without compromising quality, requires considerable time, focus, and energy. Support helps make that pace sustainable and creates more room for thoughtful development.

If BookOrbit is valuable to you and you would like to support its continued development, you can:

  • Get the official iPhone and Apple Watch app
  • Support BookOrbit on Ko-fi
  • Contribute through Open Collective
  • Star BookOrbit on GitHub

Financial support is entirely optional. Using BookOrbit, recommending it to others, or starring the repository also makes a meaningful difference.

⚠️ Unsupported Storage Configurations

Warning

NAS and network storage configurations are not supported. BookOrbit requires a local filesystem with dependable semantics for every writable path, including book libraries, import folders, application data, and PostgreSQL data. Do not place these paths on SMB/CIFS, NFS, FUSE or cloud mounts, distributed filesystems, or similar storage, even when the storage is mounted as an ordinary directory.

BookOrbit scans, moves, renames, and writes files while coordinating with its database and background jobs. Network and nonstandard filesystems can behave differently around atomic renames, locking, file notifications, permissions, caching, consistency, and durability. A configuration may appear to work and later cause intermittent failures, incomplete moves, stale library state, data loss, or corruption.

Such configurations may work in a particular environment, but using them is entirely at your own risk. No support is provided for them. Please do not open GitHub issues for problems encountered with these configurations unless the problem can be reproduced using supported local storage.

📈 Repository Activity

🌐 Translations

Help translate BookOrbit into your language on Crowdin.

When adding user-facing text in code, add the Vue I18n key only to client/src/locales/en.json. Do not edit non-English catalogs in a feature pull request; untranslated keys fall back to English until Crowdin provides a translation. See docs/LOCALIZATION.md for the complete workflow.

⭐ Star History

💬 Help and Community

  • Questions and help: Ask in GitHub Issues or browse help requests.
  • Community conversations: Start a conversation or browse community topics.
  • Bug reports: GitHub Issues
  • Feature requests: GitHub Issues
  • Security vulnerabilities: Follow the private reporting process in the Security Policy.

Questions are welcome, even if you are unsure whether something is a bug. Share workflows, your setup, or companion apps in community conversations. See the community guide for choosing a category and how topics are handled.

🔌 API Compatibility

Important

BookOrbit's API evolves alongside its official clients. Backwards compatibility is maintained for released official apps, but the API is not currently a stable public integration surface, and compatibility with third-party clients is not guaranteed. For the most reliable experience, use the official apps, OPDS, Kobo sync, or the KOReader plugin.

⚖️ License and Attribution

Copyright (C) 2025-2026 neon and BookOrbit contributors.

BookOrbit is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only.

BookOrbit material whose copyright holders have authorized them is also subject to the BookOrbit Additional Terms under sections 7(b), 7(c), 7(d), and 7(e) of the GNU AGPL v3. See the Attribution and Legal Notice for the required attribution.

releases.name: v3.6.0
releases.body:
## Highlights - **First-class comic and manga library support**: Use the one-folder-per-series layouts familiar from Kavita and Komga to identify series automatically for new and existing books.
- **Create Read Aloud books in BookOrbit**: Turn an EPUB and its audiobook into a synchronized Read Aloud edition, with background progress, guided review, and easy re-syncing.
- **First-class audiobook chapter editing**: Edit chapter titles and timing, find chapter data from Audible or the ebook, snap cu

releases.name: v3.5.0
releases.body: ## Highlights - **KOReader plugin 2.0 with four-way annotation sync**: A rebuilt widget-board interface adds richer book details, reading companions, and refreshed menus and dialogs. Highlights, notes, bookmarks, reading progress, and narration now stay in step across KOReader, Kobo, the web, and mobile clients, while an account setting can hide audiobook-only titles from the plugin catalog and bulk downloads.

releases.name: v3.4.0
releases.body:
## Highlights - **Request both formats together**: Ask for an ebook and its audiobook in one step, follow each format's progress in a grouped request, and file both into the same book. Books missing a format offer a request for the other, and ebook requests now include comic archives.
- **Follow the words while listening (iOS 1.5)**: Switch the audiobook player from Cover to Text, with Lyrics and Page layouts that highlight the narration. Read-aloud EPUBs use their timed text; downloaded audiobooks can generate transcripts on the device.

releases.name: v3.3.0
releases.body:
## Highlights - **File naming with room to work**: A new two-column workbench puts each folder on its own line, previews resolved paths against realistic book names, and shows exactly how missing metadata changes the result.
- **Approve and download books from your phone (iOS)**: Book Requests now brings the full workflow to your phone: scan an ISBN, submit or join a request, and follow its progress. Approvers can work through a dedicated queue, approve requests, compare release scores and contents, choose a download, and resolve imports, all directly in the app.
- **Enhanced CarPlay experience (iOS)**: Continue listening to downloaded or streamed aud

releases.name: v3.2.0
releases.body: ## Highlights - **BookOrbit, now made for iPad (iOS)**: The entire app has been reimagined for iPad, with spacious two-pane layouts across Home, Library, Search, Book Details, Requests, Activity, Downloads, More, and Settings, plus purpose-built EPUB, PDF, comic, and audiobook experiences with panels, spreads, search, scrubbers, keyboard shortcuts, trackpad gestures, pointer support, and a Home Screen widget.

aiSummary.whatItDoes: BookOrbit is a comprehensive self-hosted platform designed to organize and stream your personal digital library. It supports a wide variety of formats including EPUBs, PDFs, audiobooks, and comic archives, providing a unified web interface for consumption. The platform tracks reading progress across devices, offers deep metadata management, and includes native support for iOS and Apple Watch clients. By utilizing Docker for deployment, users maintain complete ownership and privacy of their reading habits and media files.

Self-hosted deployment: Provides easy installation via Docker to ensure complete data privacy.
Cross-device synchronization: Tracks reading and listening progress seamlessly across web and mobile clients.
Ecosystem integration: Offers dedicated applications for iOS and Apple Watch devices.
Metadata management: Automatically organizes the library by fetching accurate book details and covers.
